Hi Maya — attaching our completed SIG spreadsheet. Quick summary of the three items you called out:

- KMS / Key handling: Non-standard. Redwood currently manages model encryption keys; we do not support customer-supplied KMS for hosted inference in our standard offering. We describe technical controls in the attached encryption-evidence.pdf. We can offer a limited exception (customer-managed keys) only on Dedicated or Private deployments, or via an enterprise add-on with HSM integration and contract language.

- Request payload retention / logs: Non-standard. Default logging/telemetry retention for hosted API is 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for raw request payloads. We can increase retention for an enterprise contract, but longer retention of raw payloads requires a data-handling review (and in some cases, a legal addendum).

- Fine-tuning & multi-tenant isolation: Standard answer: we do not allow external fine-tuning on shared multi-tenant models; for dedicated setups we provide isolated GPU pools. That should meet your isolation requirement if you opt for Dedicated.

Attachments: SIG_Redwood_Responses_20260618.xlsx (completed questionnaire, non-standard answers highlighted), encryption-evidence.pdf (diagram + SOC2 references).

Given the two items that are "non-standard" (KMS and raw payload retention), I suspect we will need internal approval for an exception or to confirm a timeline/roadmap commitment. Karthik — can you confirm whether FinTrust is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated? Monica — we may need a quick exception assessment and potential contract language.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Sean / team — I reviewed the SIG responses and the attached encryption evidence. Short answer: we can offer a restricted exception for hosted accounts only under these conditions:

1) Scope: Customer-managed KEK supported only if the customer routes key operations through our Dedicated key proxy (private endpoint) and we provision an HSM-backed integration. This will require a short implementation project (2–4 weeks) and a security design review.

2) Compensating controls: monthly KMS usage reports, quarterly key access attestation from Redwood infra, and a 12-month exception expiry (after which we must re-evaluate). All of these must be captured in an addendum.

3) Payload retention: we can commit to a per-account retention SLA (auto-delete raw payloads after 30 days) for customers who sign the data-handling addendum; implementation work estimated 3–6 weeks to add per-account retention flags on hosted telemetry pipelines.

4) Sign-off: I will provisionally approve the exception subject to Legal and CTO review and acceptance of the proposed addendum language. Legal will need the exception form and draft contract language.

Karthik — if FinTrust is okay with a 2–4 week implementation and a 12-month exception window, this should be product feasible. Please confirm procurement timeline. Marissa — please prepare the exception-form.docx (I will provide comment track) and loop Legal (legal@redwood.com).

Monica Patel
